title: Steve Jobs on Joseph Juran: Quality as a Scientific, Repetitive Process (1991)
summary: In a 1991 interview about Dr. Joseph Juran, Jobs explains what NeXT learned about quality: treat work as repetitive processes, measure them, and let the people doing the work improve them without asking permission. Customers judge quality by experience, not marketing, and quality includes having the right product. He also praises Juran's treatment of everyone equally and his internal drive.

principles.text: Treat work as repetitive processes: instrument them, take them apart, and rebuild them to be dramatically more effective.
principles.quote: to look at everything as a repetitive process. And to instrument that process and find out how it's running and then start to take it apart and re-put it back together in ways that dramatically improve its effectiveness

principles.text: Quality starts with the product, not marketing; customers judge quality from their own experience.
principles.quote: customers don't form their opinions on quality from marketing.

principles.text: Quality means having the right, innovative product, not just flawless construction.
principles.quote: quality isn't just the product or the service; it's having the right product.

principles.text: Never accept 'that's how we've always done it'; always question what you do.
principles.quote: there is an opportunity to always question what we do.

principles.text: Put authority with the people doing the work so they improve processes without asking permission.
principles.quote: Authority should be vested in the people doing the work to improve their own processes

principles.text: Sustained contribution requires being internally driven, so praise and criticism matter less.
principles.quote: most people that are able to make a sustained contribution over time -- rather than jut a peak -- are very internally driven.
